entities.summary:
Giovanni Battista di Jacopo, known as Rosso Fiorentino or Il Rosso, was an Italian Mannerist painter who worked in oil and fresco and belonged to the Florentine school.

Born in Florence, Italy around 1494, Rosso Fiorentino began his artistic training under Domenico Ghirlandaio and later collaborated with the renowned artist Domenico Veneziano. His unique style, characterized by bold and expressive use of color, was heavily influenced by the works of the ancient Greeks and Romans.

Rosso Fiorentino's most famous works include 'The Battle of the Centaurs' and 'The Triumph of Caesar,' both of which showcase his mastery of composition and his ability to evoke powerful emotions through his art. His frescoes in the Palazzo Vecchio in Florence are considered some of the greatest examples of Mannerist art.

Rosso Fiorentino's influence can be seen in the work of later artists, including Sandro Botticelli and Raphael, who were both inspired by his innovative use of color and composition. His legacy continues to be celebrated today, with many of his works held in high esteem by art historians and enthusiasts around the world.

Despite his significant contributions to the art world, Rosso Fiorentino's life was marked by controversy and personal struggles. He was known for his fiery temper and his tumultuous relationships with his patrons and fellow artists.

In the end, Rosso Fiorentino's life was cut short when he died on November 24, 1540, at the age of 46. However, his legacy lives on, inspiring generations of artists and art lovers to this day.
